spaced-repetition drill topics it reinforces. An AI-authored lesson (`author == AI`) is not

`slides` is where the teaching now lives (GRS-0215). `body` remains the lesson's opening — what
this lesson is for and what the advisor will be able to do at the end — and is no longer
expected to carry the content on its own. Existing courses with no slides still validate; the
depth tests, not the contract, are what refuse a thin course, so a legacy course can be read

better source or fresher data. Audited/current is tight; an estimate is wide. Reported as a

Slide.description:
One slide of a lesson (GRS-0215).

The founder's standard, in their words: "A lesson is 20-40 slides of interactive detail with a
test before the next section." A slide is the unit of that. It is deliberately small — one
idea, one step, or one worked example — because the failure being corrected was lessons that
were a paragraph pretending to be a lesson.

`body` is markdown. `asset` is an inline SVG, for the same immutability reason `LessonAsset`
is: a published version that pointed at external storage would not actually be published.

course version in the first place. The renderer's own check is then a second line rather than
the only one.

StrengthRating.description:
Power strength and triad rating — ordinal with falsifiable duration semantics (§8).

Reported as a rating, NEVER as a decimal. Establishing this as an enum (not a float) is the
ADR-0002 guarantee that no decimal leaks into a triad figure.
StrengthRating.title: StrengthRating

SubcomponentRating.description:
One subcomponent's rating: a maturity level OR a first-class non-score state, never both.

Modelling this as an exclusive union is how "Not Assessed" stays distinct from a score of
zero (defect D9) — an unassessed subcomponent carries `state`, not `level`, and contributes
to no computation.
SubcomponentRating.title: SubcomponentRating

TestQuestion.description:

WidgetDef.description:
One Level-1 customer-proposition widget (ADR-0023 / GRS-0080). The 93-widget checklist is C's
Level-1 evidence layer: presence + ease/usability/depth per widget, differentiated by RARITY
(a missing Common widget is a bottleneck; a Rare widget done well scores differentiation).
`rarity` has no default — a missing/unknown value is a load-time refusal (ADR-0001).
WidgetDef.title: WidgetDef

WidgetObservation.description:
One Level-1 widget observation for the C-index grid (ADR-0023 / GRS-0083).

A widget is either PRESENT (then scored 1–5 on ease / usability / depth) or NOT present — and a
non-present widget can still carry a first-class reason it isn't a clean pass:
`PRESENT_PAYWALLED` (gated behind a paywall) or `PRESENT_DEFECTIVE` (shipped but broken).
Absent-and-nothing-else is `present=False` with no `state`. The rarity tag is NOT stored here:
it is read from the registry (a single source of truth), never copied onto the observation.
WidgetObservation.title: WidgetObservation

WinProbability.description:
A prospect's explainable win-probability (GRS-0111). ``score`` is a percentage 0–100 (a
probability, never currency — ADR-0002); ``label`` is the config-banded headline word;
``reasons`` explain what moved the estimate; ``missing_info`` names the data gaps a consultant
could fill to sharpen it. Deterministic given the prospect + config.

WizardSuggestions.title: WizardSuggestions

grassmarket__web__routers__voice_notes__.description:

A field that is present is applied with the value given — their correction, or the proposal's
own suggestion where they accepted it unchanged. A field that is **absent or null is not
applied**, whatever was proposed. There is no "accept everything" shortcut on purpose: the
approval has to name what it approves, or it is not an approval.

from the assessment's own scoring run: it is **never client-facing** (`client_facing=False`), so
it renders even for a draft wealth/exchange profile — the client-pack gate is untouched. Nothing
is persisted (a preview, not a stored deliverable). Owner-scoped and fail-loud.

Close the act-as session and hand back an ordinary admin token.

The admin's own identity is rebuilt from `acting_admin_id` rather than trusted from the client,

"candidates" is parsed as a UUID and every request 422s.

post.description:
Open an admin session scoped to one consultant (GRS-0208).

No refresh token is issued. An act-as session is deliberately short-lived and non-renewable:
it should end because the admin finished looking, not because a background refresh quietly kept
it alive for a day. Ending is `DELETE /auth/act-as`; expiry ends it too.

Self-scoped password change (GRS-0148d) — a signed-in advisor changes only their own
password. A wrong current password / OAuth-only account surfaces as 401, mirroring login.

get.description:
Google's redirect target: validate `state` against the signed cookie, exchange the code for a
Google-verified identity, resolve the invited consultant, mint the GM JWT, and hand it to the
advisory app. The JWT rides back in the URL **fragment** (never a query string; not sent to the
server) — GRS-0074 replaces this with a one-time code + `/auth/session/exchange` for the
cross-origin case.

Begin the authorization-code flow: build Google's consent URL (with `state` + PKCE) and
redirect there, stashing the state + PKCE verifier in a signed, short-TTL cookie the callback
validates. The public site's "LOG IN" simply links here.

post.description:
Authenticated consultants invite others. The raw token is returned once for out-of-band
delivery (email integration is a later loop). Only an admin may grant an elevated role/tier.

Rotate a refresh token for a new access + refresh pair (GRS-0120), so an active advisor is
not signed out at the 30-minute access TTL. A used/expired/unknown refresh token is refused
loud — the client then falls back to a full re-login.

Exchange a single-use login hand-off code for the GM JWT (GRS-0074). The only place a JWT
crosses back to the browser, over POST — never a URL. Reuse/expiry is refused loud.
